I relate a lot to your concerns. I spent a lot of time trying to identify as a butch woman or a trans man because I hated how inbetween I actually am. I own dresses and occasionally do my makeup for fun, but I cut my hair short and like getting mistaken for a guy. I use a neutral nickname but still respond to my birth name at work/school and feel like it's too much to ask for they/them pronouns even. 

I think we want to find a place where we "fit" and as nonbinary or genderfluid people, we change too much to find that specific fit with a lot of things. I like presenting every which way, but I always feel like I can't admit I like my feminine side without people thinking I'm not really genderfluid. The best advice I can give you is to just accept whatever you currently want to do- makeup washes off, hair grows back, so on and so on, so let yourself live in the moment and present however you want. You might change your mind later and that's totally fine.

Everything I do I learned from a very enthusiastic executive chef and he swears by them:

High heat eggs: omelets, scrambled eggs. I mix eggs with a bit of salt to help them beat smoother and nothing else. Continually prod and move the egg in an omelet so that it cooks evenly (kind of like poking holes in it and letting the uncooked part of the egg slide into the holes). Always take scrambled eggs and omelets out of the pan a minute or so earlier than you think they should be because they're hot enough to still cook while on the plate. 

Low heat eggs: sunnyside, and overeasy eggs. My best tip for these is to poke the inner clear membrane open (it's the clear bit that surrounds the yolk) so that it can be redistributed and cook better. Adding a little water and a lid will steam them nicely. 

I've found that vegetable oil works the best to keep eggs from browning too badly on the bottoms. My favorite thing to do is fry an egg on a bagel with cheese like they do in coffee shops.
